gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much surge the single-unit 240 V stations actually held when a named tester loaded them: HOBOTECH measured the Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus at 9,300 W on 240 V for under 5 s (rated 14,400 W), The Solar Lab held the DELTA Pro Ultra at 9,200 W for about 10 s (peak 9,300 W) and the F3800 at 8,000 W for 2-3 s, while the DELTA Pro 3 shut down after 5,100 W for about a minute; the advertised surge figures every rival page compares against a pump's locked-rotor VA are higher than these.
standout_why: Opened sparkpowered.com, wattfort.com, wattandwarden.com, batterygeneratorguide.com, homeresiliencehub.com and buyersheet.com (all cited). Each says outright it did not test any station on a pump and compares maker surge ratings (e.g. 7,680 W 'lifting' for Apex 300, 9,000 W F3800, 14,400 W Jackery) against Franklin locked-rotor tables. The only third-party measurement any of them carries is PCMag's 'sustained output above 3,800 W' for the Apex 300 (batterygeneratorguide). StorageReview's Apex 300 review (cited in pq021) measured capacity, round trip and UPS switchover but ran no surge or motor-start test. None gives a measured surge ceiling, measured idle draw or measured usable Wh for the candidates.
decides: For a 1/2 HP 240 V pump (roughly 3,000-5,500 VA start) every single-unit candidate clears even its measured ceiling, so one unit is enough and the pick can go on price and capacity. For a 1 HP or larger pump (roughly 6,000-11,500 VA start) the measured ceilings, not the ratings, decide: only the units measured holding about 9 kW (Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus at 240 V, EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra) or 8 kW briefly (F3800) are plausible on one unit, the DELTA Pro 3 (5,100 W held before shutdown) is marginal, and a soft starter becomes the cheaper fix than a second unit. Robb Sutton's one direct test (DELTA Pro 3 started a 1 HP 240 V submersible, 2,800 W peak, no soft start) shows a real pump can start well below the rated surge, so the nameplate LRA still has to be checked. The Jackery's failed 10 kW-surge AC start (The Solar Lab) is a warning against trusting its 14,400 W rating.

findings.label: Measured peak surge, 240 V and 120 V (HOBOTECH)
findings.value: 9,300 W at 240 V and 4,800 W at 120 V, each for under 5 s (rated surge 14,400 W)
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus Review: Specs, Testing, and Verdict (EcoFlow blog, 2026-10-21)
findings.note: Secondhand: EcoFlow (a competitor) summarises HOBOTECH's test; HOBOTECH's original video was not found. 9,300 / 14,400 = 65% of the rated surge. Short-duration maximum, not a motor-start test.

findings.label: Motor start and surge hold (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: Struggled to start a 10,000 W-surge air conditioner (about 3,000 W running); held 8,000 W and 9,500 W loads for about 20-30 s
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus Review: Real Competition for the Anker F3800 and DELTA Pro Ultra? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: Page shows no author or date (footer copyright 2026). Voltage of the surge test not stated. Rated surge 14,400 W.

findings.label: Measured idle draw, inverter on, no load
findings.value: About 58 W (The Solar Lab); about 85 W (HOBOTECH, via EcoFlow blog)
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus Review (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: The Solar Lab compares it with 80 W for the F3800. The 85 W HOBOTECH figure is from https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/jackery-explorer-5000-plus-review. At 58-85 W, idle alone uses about 1.4-2.0 kWh a day, more than a typical well pump's daily running energy.

findings.label: Measured surge hold (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: 9,200 W held about 10 s, brief peak 9,300 W, then shutdown (7,200 W rated continuous)
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra real-world testing (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: No author or date on the page; voltage of the surge test not stated. EcoFlow rates 10.8 kW surge (per wattandwarden.com's spec list). No well pump was tested.

findings.label: Measured idle draw (HOBOTECH)
findings.value: About 52 W, inverter on, no load
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus Review: Specs, Testing, and Verdict (EcoFlow blog)
findings.note: Secondhand via EcoFlow's own blog citing HOBOTECH's side-by-side test.

findings.label: Measured efficiency near full load (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: 59 min at just under 6,000 W, which the author rates at 98% efficiency
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra real-world testing (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: Arithmetic: about 5.9 kWh delivered from a 6,144 Wh battery. Also measured AC charging: 4 h 4 min, 7.25 kWh drawn.

findings.label: Measured surge hold and motor start (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: 8,000 W held 2-3 s; 7,200 W held about 10 s (rated 9,000 W surge); started a 3,000 W air compressor with lights flickering
findings.source_title: Putting the Anker F3800 Power Station to the Test: What Can It ACTUALLY Handle? (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: No author or date on page; voltage of surge test not stated; no 240 V load or well pump tested.

findings.label: Measured efficiency at high load (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: 37 min at 5,100 W vs 44 min expected, about 84%
findings.source_title: Putting the Anker F3800 Power Station to the Test (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: 5,100 W x 37/60 h = about 3,145 Wh delivered from 3,840 Wh rated.

findings.label: Measured usable energy and UPS switchover (StorageReview)
findings.value: 2,980 Wh delivered before inverter cutoff; switchover 13 ms to battery, 14 ms back to utility
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800: Do We Really Need Gas Generators? (StorageReview, Kevin OBrien, 2024-06-21)
findings.note: Charge 0-100% drew 4,930 Wh; switchover measured with a Quarch mains power analyzer on a ThinkStation load. 2,980 / 3,840 = 78% of rated capacity.

findings.label: Measured surge and sustained load (The Solar Lab)
findings.value: 5,100 W for nearly one minute before shutdown; loads near 6,000 W also shut it down; 3,650 W held 60 min at about 89% efficiency (rated 4,000 W / 8,000 W surge)
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 review (The Solar Lab)
findings.note: No author or date on page. The page also states the unit cannot run 240 V and 120 V outputs simultaneously (a claim, not a measurement). The 8,000 W rating was not tested as a short spike.

findings.label: 240 V well pump start (Robb Sutton)
findings.value: 1 HP 240 V submersible pump started with no soft starter, 2,800 W surge; about 3-4 h runtime
findings.source_title: EcoFlow Delta Pro 3 Review: The First True Gas Generator Killer? (Robb Sutton, 2026-02-12)
findings.note: His own three-week test; method of reading the 2,800 W not stated (likely the app display, which samples too slowly to catch locked-rotor inrush). Same table: a 3-ton central AC with a Micro-Air EasyStart tripped overload at 3,500 W. Only direct 240 V well pump test found from a named reviewer.

findings.label: Measured delivered energy, round trip and UPS switchover (StorageReview)
findings.value: 2.39 kWh delivered (86% of 2,764.8 Wh), round trip about 72%; with 2x B300K 7.38 kWh (89%); 16 ms switchover to battery in 120 V mode
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Apex 300 Review: 240V and 3,840W From One Box (StorageReview, Kevin OBrien, 2026-11-09)
findings.note: Blower-fan discharge to shutdown; recharge drew 3.30 kWh (single) and 10.01 kWh (three-pack). No surge or motor-start test in the review.

findings.label: Sustained output (PCMag, as cited by a rival)
findings.value: Above 3,800 W sustained in load tests
findings.source_title: Power Station for a Well Pump: 240V, Surge & Runtime (Battery Generator Guide)
findings.note: Secondhand: the rival page cites PCMag's Apex 300 review; PCMag's page itself was not opened. This is the one measured figure a cited rival already carries.

unsourced: A measured surge or 240 V motor start for the BLUETTI Apex 300 by a named reviewer: StorageReview, Yanko Design and the PCMag mention give none; BatterySkills claims a 1/2 HP 240 V pump test but its F3800 pages give contradictory surge figures for the same 1/3 HP pump (1,400 W, 2,900 W, 5,200 W), so it was left out as unreliable.
HOBOTECH's original test (video or article) for the Jackery 5000 Plus / DELTA Pro Ultra figures; only EcoFlow's secondhand summary was found.
Any named measurement for the EcoFlow TITAN 5000 Plus or Jackery HomePower 3600 Pro Max (surge, idle, 240 V load).

A measured 240 V well pump start on the F3800, Jackery 5000 Plus or DELTA Pro Ultra by a named reviewer: The Solar Lab, StorageReview and The Gadgeteer (Julian Perry, 2024-06-09) tested none; the Engadget/Yahoo DELTA Pro Ultra review that mentions a 240 V pump returned 403.
